extracted.intended_audience: Area Chairs / Senior Area Chairs (meta-reviewers) for machine learning conferences and journals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for Area Chairs/Senior ACs on writing clear, fair meta-reviews that summarize the paper, the review/rebuttal discussion, and make a supported accept/reject recommendation for ML conference submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summarize the paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a concise summary of the paper including its strengths and weaknesses, and add comments regarding novelty, significance, and relevance/impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give an overview of the submission's contributions and limitations so reviewers/SAC/Chairs and authors understand the core claims and the AC's interpretation of them. Mention novelty, significance, and impact explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summarize the post-rebuttal discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Report whether reviewers engaged in discussion after rebuttal, whether opinions changed, and whether scores changed (and by how much).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there was no discussion, explain why the AC made the decision anyway. For rejected papers, provide feedback to help authors improve and suggest appropriate next venues for submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include one sentence that clearly indicates your decision
rubrics_metrics.description: State clearly in one sentence the decision (e.g., 'I recommend to accept/reject this paper' or 'accept as a poster/oral').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A short explicit decision sentence helps SAC/Chairs quickly verify that the meta-review's recommendation matches its content and reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss borderline papers with Reviewers/SAC/Chairs
rubrics_metrics.description: For borderline cases, consult with reviewers, Senior ACs, or Chairs to arrive at a good decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A quick meeting often helps; if people don't respond, try email and be considerate. Offer a few open time slots to schedule meetings. You may meet reviewers/SAC/chairs separately and then consolidate opinions in the meta-review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overriding reviewers' decisions without consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not override reviewers' recommendations arbitrarily; if you must override, inform and discuss the paper with the SAC/Chairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informing SAC/Chairs and documenting the discussion avoids confusion later (e.g., if authors raise issues) because chairs can refer to your explanation and take appropriate action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid making decisions based solely on your own reading without informing reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Meta-reviewers should not replace or ignore reviewers' accounts by solely using their own reading to make decisions without notifying reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reviewers did not participate or made mistakes, first message them saying you intend to override and give them a chance to respond. In the meta-review, clearly indicate when a decision is based on your own opinion and explain why you discounted the reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Push the paper towards acceptance when reasonable
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a constructive stance: seek ways to get the work accepted at this or another appropriate venue rather than looking for reasons to reject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize authors' substantial effort and use the meta-review to help them toward acceptance; frame critiques to guide improvement and possible resubmission venues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide feedback to chairs about reviewer quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Report to SAC/Chairs any non-responsive or low-quality reviewers as well as exemplary reviewers, with brief notes on what they did wrong or well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a list and send it to SAC/Chairs so they can give feedback to reviewers and potentially improve the reviewer pool over time; include suggestions for how reviewers can improve or what they did well.
